item.title: DC shooting leaves 1 person killed, 4 injured. Gunman dead
item.description: A gunman opened fire at a gym in Washington, D.C.'s Logan Circle Thursday morning. One person has been confirmed killed and four others injured. The gunman is dead, according to police.
item.content:encoded:
A gunman opened fire at a gym in Washington, D.C.'s Logan Circle Thursday morning. One person has been confirmed killed and four others injured. The gunman is dead, according to police.

(Image credit: Tom Brenner)

item.title: Colom wins Mississippi Senate race. And, White House warns Dems over future probes
item.description: After more than a week of counting ballots, Scott Colom has narrowly won the Mississippi Senate seat. And, the White House has sent a letter warning Democrats who plan to investigate the administration.
item.content:encoded:
After more than a week of counting ballots, Scott Colom has narrowly won the Mississippi Senate seat. And, the White House has sent a letter warning Democrats who plan to investigate the administration.

(Image credit: Brandon Bell)
item.dc:creator: Brittney Melton

item.title: A blue wave helped offset for now a falling tally of Black members in the U.S. House
item.description: A Supreme Court ruling that further weakened the Voting Rights Act paved the way for a record drop in Black representation in Congress. But a midterm blue wave helped hold off such a decline for now.
item.content:encoded:
A Supreme Court ruling that further weakened the Voting Rights Act paved the way for a record drop in Black representation in Congress. But a midterm blue wave helped hold off such a decline for now.

(Image credit: Jake Crandall)
item.dc:creator: Hansi Lo Wang

item.title: At least 23 states considered laws governing ICE and schools this year
item.description: When ICE agents show up at a school, educators rely on a patchwork of policies to know what to do. This year, many state legislatures tried to update those policies.
item.content:encoded: When ICE agents show up at a school, educators rely on a patchwork of policies to know what to do. This year, many state legislatures tried to update those policies.

item.title: Senators don't always share bill text online before votes. They should, advocates say
item.description: The text of what lawmakers are considering isn't always made available for public review before it is voted on. A group of open governance advocates is calling on Senate leadership for a change.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: How Scott Colom defied the odds to go from DA to Mississippi's Democratic U.S. Senator
item.description: In a state that hasn't had a Democrat in office since 1980 and hasn't sent a Black Senator to Washington since the 1870s, Colom's win represents a massive upset in state politics.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Rep. Bennie Thompson discusses the U.S. Senate race Democrat win in Mississippi
item.description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Democratic Representative Bennie Thompson, of Mississippi, about Democrat Scott Colom's U.S. Senate victory.

item.title: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate race
item.description: Scott Colom has won the U.S. Senate race in Mississippi. After a very close race, he's the first Black man to represent the state in the Senate in nearly 150 years.

item.title: Michigan Senator-elect El Sayed discusses Democrats' ambitions
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with U.S. Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.) about his win in the midterms and what's at the top of his agenda once he begins his first term in Congress.

item.title: White House warns Trump probes could be criminal. Rep. Robert Garcia won't back down
item.description: Incoming House Oversight Committee Chairman Robert Garcia says Democrats won't be intimidated by White House threats over their planned investigations: "It's in the Constitution."
item.content:encoded:
